sections.h2: When refinishing makes more sense than replacing
body: Plenty of Lake City kitchens, whether in a 1990s subdivision house or an older home near downtown, have solid cabinet boxes with a dated finish. If the doors are sound and the layout works, cabinet refinishing in Lake City, FL changes the look without demolition. Our article on refinishing versus replacing cabinets covers the signs that a kitchen is a good candidate, and the signs that it is not.

Cabinets take more abuse than any wall, so the prep is more thorough. Doors and drawer fronts are removed and labelled, and hardware is bagged. Every surface is degreased and scuff-sanded. A bonding primer goes on so the topcoat grips factory finishes. The topcoat is a waterborne urethane enamel, which cures harder than wall paint and resists moisture and fingerprints.
bullets: Bonding primer for slick factory finishes

sections.h2: Oak grain, color choice, and matching the room
body: Oak is common in Lake City kitchens, and its open grain will show through paint unless it is filled. You can choose to keep some texture or fill it for a smoother look. Our guide to painting oak cabinets explains both options. Color can be matched from a sample door or a chip, and we test it with full-size drawdowns before spraying. If the walls need a refresh too, our Lake City interior painting crew can finish the room in the same visit.

sections.h2: Timing and keeping the kitchen usable
body: Cabinet work is indoors, so it can be scheduled any time of year, and many Lake City owners book it during the summer when exterior jobs slow down. Expect some disruption while doors are off and surfaces are curing. Before we start, the crew lead walks you through which days the kitchen will be hardest to use, so you can plan meals around them. Most projects start one to three weeks after approval, and the estimate spells out how long the kitchen will be affected. Low-VOC products are available. The project closes with a punch walk and labelled touch-up paint. For the company-wide process, see our cabinet painting and refinishing page or the Lake City contractor page.

faqs.q: Will painted cabinets hold up in a humid Lake City kitchen?
faqs.a: Yes, with the right system. Proper degreasing, a bonding primer, and a waterborne urethane enamel make a hard, moisture-resistant finish.

faqs.q: Can you paint bathroom vanities too?
faqs.a: Yes. Vanities get the same prep and enamel system as kitchen cabinets.

faqs.q: Can I keep the oak grain from showing?
faqs.a: Yes. The grain can be filled before priming for a smoother finish, or left partly visible if you like some texture.

faqs.q: Do you match a color I already have?
faqs.a: We can match from a chip, a cabinet door, or a leftover can, and you approve a full-size drawdown before spraying.
